calibration_rulings.title: The sago card name: «ساقو» (the Arabic «الساقو», letter for letter) or the reader's «ساگودانہ» used in its own description?
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d6.name, food.g0.d6.alt, food.description; every later Gulf dish whose Arabic name is the Gulf spelling of a common noun Urdu has its own word for.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B: the sago card name is «ساگودانہ» — card name, alt («اخروٹ اور پستے سے سجا ساگودانہ») and the meta description; the description keeps «چھوٹے چھوٹے ساگودانے». The Arabic «الساقو» is the Gulf spelling of the common loan ’sago’, the same noun the English writes, not a proper name: N284 (names spelled from the Arabic) binds names, and Urdu has its dictionary word for the thing (rekhta ’sago’ → «ساگو دانہ»; «سابودانہ … رک: ساگودانہ», Noun, Masculine; ur.wikipedia «ساگودانہ» 2 pages), as de, ru and zh wrote their own words. A («ساقو») refused: the on-05 reader could not tell what the card is until the folded description named «ساگودانے» (item 21); C («ساگو») is the tree in the dictionary and a place name on the reference. The proposed key «ساقو» does not enter the termbase; it is recorded for search in the entry «ساگودانہ». Masculine agreement kept («سجا»). ROUND 2: CONFIRMED by the on-r1 reader: «ساگودانہ» is familiar to him (items 1, 21).
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: «ساقو» does not occur as a whole word. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the sago card name, its alt and the snippet say «ساگودانہ».

calibration_rulings.title: Mandi: the homograph «مندی» (trade slump) — «نامی پکوان» at its first running-text mention — and the entry's gender.
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d1.pre, food.g0.d1.name, food.g0.d1.alt, food.description; the entry «مندی».
calibration_rulings.ruling: A for the text, C for the entry’s gender. «مندی نامی پکوان» once, at the first running-text mention (the device of N73 and N292 for a name that reads as an Urdu word; the press tag mixes the dish with the trade slump); the card name, the alt and the meta list stay bare (headings and alts are outside N292; the snippet is a list of dish names). The on-05 reader read the dish without a slump reading (items 6–9). GENDER: feminine, PENDING — the morphology of a loan in «ی» and one weak press agreement; stage 1’s masculine rested only on the hypernym «پکوان». Not exercised: every agreeing word follows «پکوان» or «تھال» (round 2 keeps that: «مندی نامی پکوان کو … رکھا جاتا ہے»). B refused (the slump reading as the subject). ROUND 2: Contested by one reader: the on-r1 reader read the bare heading «مندی» as the slump first and resolved it from the kicker (item 7, moderate). Headings stay outside the «نامی» device; charged under fit.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «مندی» in running text first stands as «مندی نامی پکوان»; a verb or adjective that would agree with «مندی» itself is raised, not written, while the entry is pending.

calibration_rulings.title: The red-bread sentence «یہ “لال روٹی” (خبز احمر) بھی کہلاتی ہے۔»: the Urdu-script transliteration, the marks, and «لال» or «سرخ».
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d7.pre; the entry «خبز احمر»; the C5b pair.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «یہ “لال روٹی” (خبز احمر) بھی کہلاتی ہے۔» — the alias both sources quote, in marks (N72, N113), in the English’s order, the transliteration the English carries written in Urdu script from the Arabic «الخبز الأحمر» (article dropped, N284; P11), as the three earlier lines kept theirs; «لال» over «سرخ» (the everyday colour word of the kitchen). The naming verb «کہلاتی» is feminine by «روٹی» (N107/N170 frame). The on-05 reader understood both as names of one bread (item 24); the bracket’s purpose unsignalled is minor. C («“خبز احمر” (لال روٹی)») stays on record as the fallback; B drops a name the English carries; D («سرخ») not taken. C5b SYNONYM_PAIRS (coordinator, after stage 7): «کھجور کی روٹی» ↔ «لال روٹی». ROUND 2: Both readers read the marks as an alternative name; both found the bracket unsignalled (minor). A stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the date-bread card carries «“لال روٹی” (خبز احمر)» once, in its naming clause.

calibration_rulings.title: Gender of «گندم» (wheat): the dictionary says masculine, the reference and the press of Pakistan agree in the feminine.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «گندم» agrees in the FEMININE («دلی ہوئی گندم», «… پکتی ہے»), the usage of the reference’s own article on wheat and of its verbs of cultivation (stage 4, HTTP 200); rekhta’s masculine is recorded in the entry as the dissent, as N287 recorded it for «کھجور». The entry stays PENDING until the Urdu Lughat is read (unreachable at stage 4). The on-05 reader called «دلی ہوئی گندم» the right Urdu (item 2). ROUND 2: No remark from the on-r1 reader.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «گندم» agrees in the feminine.

calibration_rulings.title: «جریش» in the mufallaq description: the reference article on harees gives «جریش» as another name of harees; here it is the grain.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «دلی ہوئی گندم (جریش)» — the term in the source’s bracket directly after its Urdu meaning, so the page gives it the grain sense; B drops a term both sources carry, C is heavier. The on-05 reader took «(جریش)» for the local name of the cracked wheat (item 12) — the sense intended. Entry pending (no Urdu attestation in the grain sense; the reference’s dish sense, another name of harees, recorded in its note). ROUND 2: The on-r1 reader was unsure of the bracket’s purpose (item 13, minor); the on-05 reader took it rightly. A stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «جریش» stands only in its bracket after «دلی ہوئی گندم».

calibration_rulings.title: methodP2 without the loan «کارڈ»: «اس صفحے کے چار پکوانوں کے تعارف میں» — does it still say that four CARDS mention the occasions?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «اس صفحے کے چار پکوانوں کے تعارف میں …» — the count kept, the mention placed in each dish’s introduction; no loan. The on-05 reader tied the sentence to four of the dishes (item 27); his difficulty in matching four occasions to four dishes is the source’s (logged). Round 1 gives the next sentence the plural that points back to the four («ان پکوانوں», change 7). B stays the fallback; C («کارڈ») refused under P16. ROUND 2: The on-r1 reader charged the note’s register and the unnamed four dishes (item 28): the source’s; A stands.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: methodP2 keeps «چار» and the four occasions; «کارڈ» is not written.

calibration_rulings.title: Omelette (balaleet alt, AR «مقلاة العجة»): the native «خاگینہ» or the loan «آملیٹ» (P16).
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «خاگینے کی کڑاہی» — the native headword (rekhta, Noun, Masculine, ’omelette’) satisfies P16; the on-05 reader read it as the omelette pan without a stumble (item 14). B (the loan «آملیٹ») refused while the native word is read; C («انڈے تلنے کی کڑاہی») stays the fallback. Entry verified. ROUND 2: No remark on «خاگینہ» from the on-r1 reader (item 15 is the egg the description omits, source).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: «آملیٹ» is not written.

calibration_rulings.title: food.dineCta leads to the ENGLISH restaurants index: should the Urdu label say so?
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «یہ پکوان کہاں چکھیں؟ کھانے پینے کی جگہیں دیکھیں ←», no language note: the note is not in the source string, the Russian line that faced the same English target added none, and the approved Urdu links do not mark English targets. The on-05 reader found the link clear, natural and useful (item 30); he did not follow it. FOR THE COORDINATOR / OWNER, one line: the link opens the English restaurants index; a site-wide marker for English targets on /ur/ (e.g. «(انگریزی میں)») is a decision for the whole interface, not this string. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED by both readers (on-r1 item 30).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the dineCta label is the approved «کھانے پینے کی جگہیں» with the arrow «←».

calibration_rulings.title: Tomato sauce in the rice card: «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» — the on-05 reader pictured a chutney cooked into the rice (item 5, moderate); stage 5 reported «ٹماٹر» as an English-origin word without a termbase entry (checklist item 9).
calibration_rulings.ruling: C (round 2): the rice card names «ٹماٹر» alone — «… گوشت یا مرغی، ٹماٹر اور مسالوں (…) کے ساتھ …». Two readers of two read «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» (round 1’s A) as the side chutney, and the reference’s own article defines it so: a misreading of what goes into the dish outweighs the loss of the form ’sauce’, which is charged under accuracy. B refused under P16 (no entry; a native wording exists); D refused: «مسالا» beside «مسالوں» in the same list reads as the spices. «ٹماٹر» is an English loan with its own Urdu headword and gender (Rekhta, Origin English, Noun Masculine) and no native competitor: P16 is satisfied by the headword, as N126 ruled for «کیتلی»; entered verified as «ٹماٹر» (addendum to round 2). Round 1’s pending entry «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی» is withdrawn (never in the termbase); a real tomato chutney on a later page is still «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی».
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the string «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی اور مسالوں» does not occur. For the proofreader, not machine-read: tomato sauce cooked into a dish is «ٹماٹر»; «ساس», «پیسٹ», «گریوی» are not written; a tomato chutney served on the side is still «ٹماٹر کی چٹنی».
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge's addendum to that round

calibration_rulings.title: An image of the source that the Urdu renders with a fixed phrase of another sense, or literally enough to mislead: mandi ’not so much cooked as entrusted to the earth, the way secrets are’ (AR «لا يُطهى … بل يُستودَع في باطن الأرض كما تُستودَع الأسرار»).
calibration_rulings.binds: food.g0.d1.pre; any later figure of the source whose literal Urdu is a fixed idiom of another sense.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D (round 2): the image stays; no wording of it reads as burial or as undercooking. (1) Where an Urdu fixed phrase carries a sense the source’s image does not (burial: «زمین کے سپرد», «امانت» in the earth), the image is said in the source’s own terms — the Arabic’s, the authority: in the depth of the earth, kept as a secret is kept. (2) Where the literal form of a contrast measures what the source only ranks (’not so much cooked as’ → «پکایا کم جاتا ہے», read as ’little cooked’), the contrast ranks: «پکانے سے بڑھ کر». The verb is «سنبھال کر رکھنا» (to keep with care, the frame of a secret kept); the ’trust’ nuance of «يُستودَع» is what leaves, charged under accuracy. A and B are withdrawn; C refused (adding information; the method is logged as the source’s). D is unread until the r2 blind read.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: none of «زمین کے سپرد», «میں امانت زیادہ رکھا», «راز امانت رکھے», «پکایا کم جاتا ہے» occurs. For the proofreader, not machine-read: the mandi image keeps the source’s ranking (the keeping above the cooking) and adds no method. The guard bans the withdrawn wordings of this one image, not the words «امانت» or «تہہ» elsewhere; the spelling «تہ» of this page follows the approved site text and is not ruled site-wide here.
calibration_rulings.ruled_by: Judge round2, b19-ui (round 4), 2026-10-15; record corrected by the judge's addendum to that round
